rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for a small amount of something.

example.english: I only want a little sugar.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 jiu3 siu2 siu2 tong4 zau6 gau3 laa3

rows.note: Use this after the thing concerned, especially when saying that not much of it remains or is available.

example.english: There is little milk left in the fridge.
example.traditional: 雪櫃入面啲牛奶唔多喇。
example.jyutping: syut3 gwai6 jap6 min6 dik1 ngau4 naai5 m4 do1 laa3

rows.note: Use this for a small amount in a positive context, when the exact smallness is less emphatic than with 少少.

example.english: Give me a little time and I will get it done.
example.traditional: 畀我一啲時間，我就搞掂喇。
example.jyutping: bei2 ngo5 jat1 di1 si4 gaan3 ngo5 zau6 gaau2 dim6 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for saying that the amount is not much.

example.jyutping: ni1 dou6 ge3 wai2 m4 do1

rows.note: Use this for a small amount when the amount itself is being referred to, as in knowing or having a little.

example.jyutping: ngo5 sik1 siu2 siu2 gwong2 dung1 waa2

rows.note: Use this when stressing that the amount is very small, especially in phrases such as ‘know very little’.

example.english: I know very little about this area.
example.jyutping: ngo5 deoi3 ni1 fong1 min6 sik1 dak1 hou2 siu2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for saying that something is not much or happens to only a small degree.
Use this before an adjective or verb when little means “not very” or “not much,” especially in negative evaluations.

example.jyutping: keoi5 m4 hai6 gei2 sik1 zyu2 faan6

rows.note: Use this after a verb or adjective to stress that the difference or increase is small, as in “only a little faster.”

example.english: This new car is faster than the old one, but only a little.
example.traditional: 呢部新車快過舊嗰部，快得唔多。
example.jyutping: ni1 bou6 san1 ce1 faai3 gwo3 gau6 go2 bou6 faai3 dak1 m4 do1

rows.note: Use this for a small positive degree, especially when something is slightly more or less than before, as in 快少少.

example.jyutping: nei5 haang4 faai3 siu2 siu2 laa1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something physically small or for a young child, as in 細路仔.

example.jyutping: ni1 zek3 sai3 gau2 hou2 dak1 ji3

rows.note: Use 少少 for a small amount or number, including a short or limited amount of time, as in 少少時間 or 得少少人.

example.english: I only have a little time.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dak1 siu2 siu2 si4 gaan3 zaa3

rows.note: Use this when little means unimportant or of little significance rather than physically small.

example.jyutping: ni1 go3 sai3 zit3 m4 zung6 jiu3

rows.note: Use 細 before a kinship term to specify the younger sibling or younger relative, such as 細妹 or 細佬.

example.english: My little sister is in secondary school this year.
example.jyutping: ngo5 sai3 mui6 gam1 nin4 duk6 zung1 hok6
